items.Description: Created by an unknown druid, the Ring of the Elements offers an inherent, though minor, protection against elemental attacks. In addition, however, it provides the wearer with an increased defense that can be called upon once each day.

items.Name: Ring of the Nightdancers
items.Description: This seemingly ornamental band is in fact the symbol of the Nightdancers, informing anyone within the guild that the wearer is a fellow member.  In addition, it has been magically imbued with several enhancements to aid a rogue in his or her career.

items.Name: Ring of the Protector
items.Description: A relic from the Deshandrean Empire, this ring was created for Emperor Gallius II, to be used when he led his armies against the Dreighul invaders. items.Name: Ring of Tyrsis Orr
items.Description: Tyrsis Orr, the renowned wizard of the Order of the Moon, was equally famed for his item-crafting abilities.  He created this ring for personal use to enhance his already impressive magical abilities.

items.Name: Rivald's Surprise
items.Description: Rivald Ondellor was a man who disliked conspicuousness.  He never bragged about his abilities--potent though they were--and spoke in a soft voice. items.Name: Robes of Orith
items.Description: The name of Orith is well-known to nearly every magic-wielder in the world, but is seldom spoken outside such arcane circles. items.Name: Rodigar's Missive
items.Description: These documents are stamped with Prince Rodigar's personal seal.  Whatever is written inside must be of the utmost importance.

items.Name: Rod of Dispelling
items.Description: A staple of wizards everywhere, these items have been put to excellent use against magical traps, spells, and even creatures.

items.Name: Rod of Life
items.Description: One of the most prized possessions of any faith, the Rod of Life has become the mark of the most devoted--and most favored--of priests. items.Name: Rogue's Companion
items.Description: The true name and purpose of this shortsword have long since been lost to history, but it is now known by its new application--the preferred weapon of the rogue. items.Name: Rogue's Ring
items.Description: A favorite of many criminals, this ring aids a wearer in escaping detection.  It is also used by those adventurers who prefer to avoid unnecessary combat.

items.Name: Roof Key
items.Description: This key unlocks the door for the stairwell that lets out onto the building's rooftop.

items.Name: Rusty Key
items.Description: According to Faelred, this rusty key was found on the body of a man believed to be aiding those who poisoned King Aelfrecht.  Faelred believes it may allow you to enter the conspirators' hideout in the southwestern part of the Wolfgate.

items.Name: Rymencor's Call
items.Description: Rymencor, a druid of no small renown, is said to have fashioned this staff from a mighty oak in his forest home.  According to legend, a lightning bolt struck the oak during a storm, attracting the notice of the local forest animals.  As Rymencor followed the animals and watched…

items.Description: This key belonged to Salime, the proprietress of the Healing Hands shop in Alderment's Square.

items.Description: This is the key to your room at the Scribbler's Quill Inn, located in the University District of Deornhal.

items.Description: This scroll has been imbued with a holy invocation similar to the Rite of Transference.  Using this scroll's power will bind the bearer's soul to the current location.  At the very instant before death, the bearer will be transferred back to the location at which the scroll was …

items.Description: Harkening from the desert kingdom of Dembia, Searing Wind's best known wielder was the hero-nomad Khaliman Sebar. items.Name: Shadow Mask
items.Description: This helmet, fashioned from some lightweight, ebony-hued metal, is simple and unadorned in construction.  Its true nature is revealed once it is actually worn, allowing its possessor to--for all intents and purposes--disappear into thin air.

items.Description: Ramon-Uht was a Tsuyanan hero most renowned for hunting down and slaying the ferocious Beast of Kappigra. items.Name: Shield Staff
items.Description: Fashioned by the wizard-smiths of Orith's Hold, these magic staves have been enchanted with several virtues to help their bearers better protect themselves from physical attacks--a welcome ability indeed for the fighting-deficient wizard or sorcerer.

items.Name: Shimmering Plate
items.Description: Created as a succession gift for King Aelfstan III by the King of Ronne, this suit of golden armor became a beloved heirloom for the royal family for generations. items.Description: This log book contains a list of ships that have entered Deornhal's port, a record of their arrival and departure dates, port of call, and a summary of their goods.  There does not seem to be any information immediately useful to you.

items.Name: Ship Manifest for The Sea Dog
items.Description: This ship manifest is dated for the prior week and details the cargo for a ship called The Sea Dog, mastered by a Captain Krigor. items.Name: Silver Circlet Key
items.Description: This is the key to your room at the Riverside District inn, the Silver Circlet.

items.Name: Silver Scales
items.Description: Fashioned ages ago for Sir Kerris, a stalwart knight in service to Dergarion, this suit of scale mail is made entirely from silver links and enhanced by magic to ward off the blows of the God of Justice's enemies.  An unexpected side effect of this virtue is to increase the wear…

This letter was found on Sir Greyard's person.  It reads:

"Greyard,

items.Description: This bloody mass was once the head of the horrific creature that was terrorizing the sewers beneath Alderment's Square.

items.Name: Slavers' Key
items.Description: This copper key was found on the body of the slaver leader.  You suspect it will open the cells holding the captured children.

items.Name: Sleeping Tiger
items.Description: Crafted by the monk-smith Tomigashi Rikku, this kama has been enchanted with the abilities exemplifying the "Way of the Sleeping Tiger," a warrior code which teaches that no movement should be wasted, and when action *is* called for, such action must be focused and forceful.

items.Name: Smuggler's Key
items.Description: Found on the leader of the smuggling operation in Deornhal, this key undoubtedly unlocks a door or chest that he believed valuable enough to be protected from the rest of his comrades.

items.Name: Smuggler's Map
items.Description: This map seems to detail the location of a small island not far from Deornhal.  Judging by the inlets and hidden coves around the island, you get the impression that it would make an excellent hideout for pirates, smugglers, and the sort.

items.Name: Soldier's Ring
items.Description: This simple copper band has been imbued with a minor magical virtue that resists attacks made by swords and axes. items.Name: Sorcerers' Key
items.Description: This key was found on the body of a slain sorcerer, and may be needed to gain access to their secret lair.

items.Description: So named because of the grief and lust for vengeance of its original wielder, Sorrow's Herald has struck down many a foe. items.Description:
No one knows when or how Soulfire was created, but it first appeared in legend when it was given to the young warrior Enkaro Dhont by the mysterious Green Wizard of Hawkbeak Mountain, before the lad was sent into the Otherworld in search of his abducted love, Oricia.

items.Description: Named for the ancient kingdom that once worshipped the Death God Agel'lor, this staff was created for and wielded by only one owner--the wizard-warrior known only as the Bane of Agremmon. items.Name: Stinging Needles
items.Description: When contact is made with a target, these enchanted darts cause a nearly overwhelming stinging sensation that quickly renders the victim's body temporarily useless.

items.Name: Storm Flail
items.Description: The origins of this weapon are unknown, although it is commonly suspected to have originated in Greyholm.  For a time it was wielded by the High Patriarch of the Temple of Hostenos, Lord of Storms, until it was passed on to a wandering paladin and lost in battle.

items.Description: Created at Duke Aedelred's behest, Summer's Heat is intended to be a companion piece to the shortsword Winter's Bite.  Both weapons are formidable in their own right, but used together provide an offensive barrage that few can stand against.

items.Name: Sword of the Pariah
items.Description: Wielded by the exiled warrior Mindohar, this magical scimitar has come to symbolize the curse of injustice and loneliness. items.Description: This pouch, taken from Talbot, contains one hundred gold pieces.

items.Name: Talon of the White Hawk
items.Description: An ancient weapon said to have been forged in the time of the Deshandrean Empire, this longbow has weathered time and use to remain in near-perfect condition. items.Name: Tarnished Silver Necklace
items.Description:
This silver necklace is tarnished with age, but you can still read the inscription engraved upon its back:

"To Amelia, with all my love.

--M."

items.Name: Telleriand
items.Description: Wielded by the famed mage-hunter Rymar od'Vaddoch, this sword has become notorious among the spell-casting community--so much so that, even four hundred years after Rymar's death, the name "Telleriand" is still spoken of only in whispers.

items.Name: Temple of Agel'lor Key
items.Description: This key was given to you by the High Matriarch of the Temple of Irime.  According to her, it will unlock the door leading into the hidden lair of the cultists of Agel’lor.

items.Name: The Hrisgeld Prophecies
items.Description:
Parts of this book have decayed with age, but the majority of it is still intact.  Thumbing through the pages, you see countless rambling "prophecies" painstakingly copied from the collected notes of a man named Hrisgeld.

items.Description: For the first few centuries of Elondria's existence, politics were a relatively simple affair.  The king held absolute authority over his subjects and answered to no one. items.Name: Thief's Ring
items.Description: Rings of this nature are often employed to enhance an individual's criminal skills--especially those who know their skills to be inadequate to the task.

items.Description: According to legend, the Thresher of Lives was fashioned for a death-cult priest named Aggrivore.  Covered in spikes, the heavy flail was already an intimidating weapon. items.Description: This is a torn piece of cloth that looks like it caught on a nail sticking up out of the floorboard.  It is the same color as Contessa's dress.  Perhaps she passed this way in her haste to escape.

items.Name: Torrant's Ruby Ring
items.Description: This ring--a blood red ruby mounted upon a gold band, surrounded by tiny emeralds--seems to be of exquisite craftsmanship.  Something about it, however, seems a little strange, although you can't quite but your finger on it.

items.Name: Traveler's Cloak
items.Description: Cloaks of this nature have been imbued with a simple enchantment that protects the wearer from the ravages of ill weather.  Although its original intentions may never be known, it has now become a favorite item among wayfarers of all kinds, thus earning it its current name.

items.Description: It is said that Elstan, a timid young farmer, was given this helm when a ghostly apparition claiming to have been sent by Ulgard appeared before him, warning him of an attack on his village by Rimmen'sae marauders. items.Description:
Wielded by Gretta the Vengeful, a single-minded woman whose quest to avenge her slain love led her on a years-long search for the mighty warrior known only as Darkheart, this axe became the symbol of the strength of her determination.

items.Name: Vorliss Cellar Key
items.Description: This key must be the one Nedric the butler was referring to.  It will probably allow you access to the cellars beneath the Vorliss estate.

items.Name: Vorliss House Key
items.Description: This key will allow you to unlock most doors throughout the Vorliss estate.

items.Name: Wagging Tongue
items.Description:
Once wielded by the mercenary Falvahar Flame-hair, surviving foes soon nicknamed this weapon after the warrior's penchant for seemingly never-ending monologues, witticisms, and ramblings--even during the heat of battle.

items.Description: Created as a contingency for mages who had expended their spell reservoirs, wands like this one have often provided an unpleasant surprise for their user's foes.

items.Name: Wand of Ice

items.Name: Wand of Trap Detection
items.Description: Wands of this nature were created to assist adventurers of all types, although they have also gained favor among rogues and assassins whose trap-detection abilities may be somewhat...lacking.

items.Name: War Robes of Eman Varr
items.Description: Allegedly worn by the wizard-lord Eman Varr as he led his troops into one victorious battle after another, these robes were lost upon his death at the hands of a rival necromancer.

items.Name: Watcher's Inn Room Key
items.Description: This heavy key unlocks the door to the room you've rented at the Watcher's Inn, the hostelry located in the Administrative District.

items.Name: Wayfarer's Staff
items.Description: Fashioned from a shaft of fire-hardened ironwood, the Wayfarer's Staff was enchanted with the lone traveler in mind. items.Name: Weary Wanderer Key
items.Description: This key unlocks the door to the room you rented at the Weary Wanderer Inn in the Boar's Gate District.

items.Name: Welcoming Hearth Room Key
items.Description: This is the key to the room you've rented at the Welcoming Hearth, the inn in Alderment's Square.

items.Name: Whelm
items.Description: A powerful weapon wielded by the mighty paladin Junorich Mynroddin, this hammer has been imbued with the ability to strike fear into the hearts of those it strikes. items.Description:
This whetstone, which appears to the eye to be nothing out of the ordinary, once belonged to Sir Lothwynn, a knight of Khovanion.

items.Description: A traveling Tsuyanan monk named Shingai used to carry this impressive weapon with him during his journeys. items.Description: Long the symbol of the famed Knights of Narromae, the White Blade came to be feared among the creatures of evil.  Unfortunately, a concerted attack against the Fortress of the Sun by the Dreighul resulted in the death of the Lord Commander--the traditional wielder of the White B…

items.Name: White Power Rod
items.Description: This piece of crystal, little larger than your fist, hums almost at the edge of hearing and gives off a soft, white glow.  Even before you touch it, you can sense its magical nature.

items.Name: Wicked Wench Key
items.Description: This is the key to your room at the Wicked Wench Inn.

items.Name: Widow's Grief
items.Description: Wielded by the blackguard Alvygar of Rimmen'sae, this blade's name was born out of the many battles that witnessed its use.  Invariably Alvygar would cut a bloody swath through those who opposed him, leaving behind nothing but "a widow's grief."

items.Name: Wilhelm's Writ of Passage
items.Description: This sealed document, signed by High Patriarch Wilhelm of the Ulgard Temple, orders the guards stationed at the Pennytown gate to allow you free passage to the lichyards beyond.

items.Name: Windsong
items.Description: Named for the sound made by the rapidly firing arrows loosed from this shortbow, Windsong bestows upon its wielder the virtue of haste, enabling him or her to send a volley of arrows into the air in the time it would take a normal archer to fire but one or two.

items.Name: Winter Ring
items.Description: Created by the mad wizard Kemmehan, this ring empowers the wearer with an increased resistance to cold-based attacks--and is capable of delivering one of its own.  Unfortunately, it has the added disadvantage of making the wearer especially vulnerable to fire.
PropertiesDecoded: Cone of Cold (9) Cast Spell 1 Use/Day

items.Name: Winter's Bite
items.Description: The mate to the longsword Summer's Heat, Winter's Bite was forged specifically for Duke Aedelred.  Each weapon is a powerful magic relic in its own right, but when wielded together in the hands of a skilled warrior, the two become virtually unstoppable.

items.Name: Wulfstan's Key
items.Description: This key was given to you by Sir Alain, a member of the Sworn Brothers.  Supposedly it will open the door to Sir Wulfstan's home, located in the northeastern section of the Godsway.
